scope_amendments.authorized_by: lead-engineer decision (2026-09-06), after the task 13 builder stopped rather than edit a path the allowlist did not contain.
scope_amendments.reason: Task 13 adds `vestrace worker --once`, a bounded cycle observable from outside the process. The argument belongs on the `Command::Worker` Clap variant and its dispatch arm, both in `crates/vestrace-cli/src/main.rs:361`, which the allowlist did not contain — `crates/vestrace-cli/src/commands/worker.rs` did. The task brief asserted main.rs was in scope; that assertion was not checked and was wrong. The builder refused to proceed, which is the behaviour the standing rule requires. The test is a new file because the wiring must be proved by launching the binary through `CARGO_BIN_EXE_vestrace`, not by reading source text: `crates/vestrace-cli/tests/provider_runtime_wiring.rs` asserts on `include_str!` substrings, which can prove a forbidden name is absent and can never prove a handler was registered.
scope_amendments.consequence: Two paths. The Clap variant gains one optional flag and the dispatch arm passes it through; no other command changes. The new test asserts three exit codes — work done, none found, poll failed — because the existing polls convert a failure into `false` (`worker.rs:391`, `:480`), so a two-outcome interface would report a database failure as no work. Recorded as an amendment rather than a silent widening because the reason is worth keeping visible: the brief stated a scope membership it had not verified, and the guard caught it rather than the reviewer.
